class="entry-title">The Easiest Savory Oatmeal</h1></header><div class="entry-content"><p>Did anyone else forget how to keep a calendar during the pandemic? Because I wasn’t scheduling things for over a year, I sort of forgot how to keep my calendar organized. My summer has quickly filled up with so many travel plans, and between all that excitement, I’ve definitely forgotten about a few things I’ve needed to do. Like, you know, post on my blog? I think this is the first time I went over a week and <em>completely </em>forgot about it. Anyways, here I am today, back in action, to tell you all about savory oatmeal. So let’s get into it, shall we?</p><span id="more-7686"></span><figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img width="1200" height="1800" src="https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-1-kiersten-hickman.jpg" alt="savory oatmeal in a bowl with egg and cooked veggies" class="wp-image-7687" srcset="https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-1-kiersten-hickman.jpg 1200w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-1-kiersten-hickman-200x300.jpg 200w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-1-kiersten-hickman-683x1024.jpg 683w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-1-kiersten-hickman-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-1-kiersten-hickman-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-1-kiersten-hickman-560x840.jpg 560w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-1-kiersten-hickman-150x225.jpg 150w" sizes="(max-width: 1200px) 100vw, 1200px" /></figure><p>Don’t be alarmed by the phrase “savory oatmeal.” At first, I was put off by the idea of it…until I tried it. Typically when one makes a bowl of oatmeal it’s full of all sorts of delicious sweet things—fruit, peanut butter, maple syrup, and more. But the idea of savory oatmeal is to top the bowl of oats with all kinds of savory toppings—like eggs, vegetables, and breakfast meats.</p><p>I usually gravitate towards eating a bowl of sweet oatmeal (particularly a bowl of my favorite <a href="https://www.kierstenhickman.com/peanut-butter-overnight-oats-recipe/">overnight oats</a>, or <a href="https://www.kierstenhickman.com/pumpkin-oatmeal-recipe/">pumpkin oatmeal</a>). But given that I didn’t have <em>any </em>fruit in the fridge the other day and I was craving a bowl of oatmeal after a hard workout, I decided to give savory oatmeal a try. And I was not disappointed.</p><p>So cooking a bowl of savory oats is similar to cooking a bowl of sweet oats at first. You cook <strong>1/2 cup of rolled cut oats </strong>with <strong>1 cup of water or milk </strong>over a stovetop. You could also use unsweetened almond milk, which is typically what I gravitate towards when making a bowl of oatmeal.</p><p>Once the oatmeal is cooked, you throw it in a bowl and top it with your savory toppings. The savory toppings will likely need to be cooked in a separate pan while cooking up the oats in a pot. Oats take about 3 to 5 minutes to cook over the stove, so be sure to time accordingly based on the toppings you would like to make.</p><p>Some ideas for <strong>savory oatmeal toppings </strong>include:</p><ul><li>Eggs</li><li>Bacon</li><li>Breakfast sausage (pork, turkey, or chicken)</li><li>Pork roll</li><li>Garlic</li><li>Spinach</li><li>Bell peppers</li><li>Onions</li><li>Tomatoes</li><li>Cheese</li><li>Hot sauce</li></ul><figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" width="1200" height="1800" src="https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-2-kiersten-hickman.jpg" alt="savory oatmeal in a bowl with eggs veggies and hot sauce" class="wp-image-7688" srcset="https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-2-kiersten-hickman.jpg 1200w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-2-kiersten-hickman-200x300.jpg 200w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-2-kiersten-hickman-683x1024.jpg 683w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-2-kiersten-hickman-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-2-kiersten-hickman-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-2-kiersten-hickman-560x840.jpg 560w, https://www.kierstenhickman.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/savory-oatmeal-2-kiersten-hickman-150x225.jpg 150w" sizes="(max-width: 1200px) 100vw, 1200px" /></figure><p>Honestly, toppings for savory oatmeal can work similarly to fill-ins for an omelet. Think of your favorite omelet you love to make, and throw those types of fillings on top of your bowl of oats.</p><p>You can also throw some fresh vegetables on top that aren’t cooked, like a handful of arugula, pico de gallo, or sliced avocado. </p><p>Here’s a combination I recently made that I really enjoyed recently. But again, you can make your savory oatmeal however you want! This is just me writing a blog post to inspire you to try a bowl of savory oatmeal this week.
